I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on all my land. In Quzhou County, that is the most dependable way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and avoid taking risks with crops that need more skill, more labor, or a less certain buyer. At the start of this season, my wheat is already in the field from autumn sowing, so my job now is to carry that wheat through spring water and fertilizer, harvest it in early summer, and then sow maize right after harvest so I do not lose soil moisture or time. I will use improved or hybrid seed rather than old saved seed because I want steadier emergence and yield, but I will not chase very high input farming because fertilizer, water, and pesticides all cost money. I will plough before wheat when I can, then use rotary tillage for the quick turnover into summer maize. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in my area depends more on spring water, and I will keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed because too many applications raise cost fast. I am choosing a simple, familiar, two-crop plan that fits my age, my experience, and the conditions I farm in.
